title: The Triumph of Tech-Fueled Propaganda
gist: Teaser of a Renée DiResta and Josh A. Goldstein essay warning the US is unprepared for a new wave of tech-fueled foreign influence operations. It opens with hundreds of hijacked Bluesky accounts used in April and May to push Ukraine content, attributed by Clemson University researchers to Russia's US-sanctioned Social Design Agency, whose broader operations were exposed by leaked documents.

themes.theme: Russian influence operations on social platforms

insights.claim: In April and May 2026, hundreds of Bluesky users found their accounts hijacked and used to spread Ukraine-related content, a campaign Clemson University researchers attributed to Russia's Social Design Agency.
insights.so_what: Account-takeover influence ops create trust-and-safety and reputational risk for social platforms.
insights.quote: hundreds of users of the social media platform Bluesky discovered that their accounts had been hijacked and used to spread content about Ukraine.
insights.locator: In April and May, hundreds of users
insights.speaker: Renée DiResta

insights.claim: The Social Design Agency is a Russian consulting firm sanctioned by the US Treasury for running Kremlin-directed malign influence campaigns, and the Bluesky effort was only one piece of its larger portfolio.
insights.so_what: Sanctions have not halted state-linked influence contractors.
insights.quote: The Bluesky effort turned out to be only one piece of the SDA’s much larger portfolio of recent operations
insights.locator: Researchers at Clemson University later attributed
insights.speaker: Renée DiResta

insights.claim: Leaked Social Design Agency documents obtained by Delfi Estonia and shared with the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project revealed plans for further operations.
entities: Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project
